title: Sampling policy feedback controller to stabilize trace throughput and reduce hotpath overhead
creator: Ayesha Patel
description: Problem: tracing hotpaths are causing per-request allocation spikes and increasing p99 request latency under high QPS. Current adaptive/tail samplers operate asynchronously and sometimes overcommit reservoir capacity for a few services, which amplifies allocator pressure on the hot path and creates noisy telemetry. Goal: introduce a lightweight feedback controller that continuously reconciles desired sampled-span emit rates per service/route with actual emitted rates and adjusts ingress sampling weights with minimal on-path overhead. Approach: (1) collect local emit_rate, reservoir_utilization, recent_error_rate, and tail_latency_ratio as compact counters at each ingress agent; (2) aggregate these into a short-window moving average in the control plane; (3) compute per-service weight adjustments via a damped proportional controller with safety floor/ceiling and fairness credits for low-cardinality customers; (4) publish tiny delta updates to ingress proxies (gRPC push) keyed by service + environment. This hybrid deterministic/probabilistic scheme preserves guaranteed retention for error/timeout traces while reducing non-actionable span emission by targeting high-volume low-value traffic. Implementation notes: controller will be implemented as a small Rust process in the observability control plane; ingress agent change is ~40 LOC to apply updated weight multipliers and keep a deterministic fast-path for error spans. Feature will be behind a rollout flag and default to conservative knobs.
updates: 2026-01-20: Spike detection algorithm prototyped in Python. Early bench shows controller can bring emitted spans per-second down by ~34% under synthetic burst while keeping error trace retention stable.

2026-01-26: Design review with PM/Infra. Decided to use damped proportional controller with update interval of 5s and exponential backoff hysteresis to avoid oscillation. Confluence design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Sampling+Policy+Feedback+Controller

2026-02-02: Implemented ingress-side no-allocation fast-path for retained error spans (deterministic keep). Microbench in dev cluster: per-request allocations reduced by 42% for sampled code path. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/9876

2026-02-05: Load test (1M rps) in perf lab with mixed traffic. Observed improved p99 request latency by 18% on ingress and 25% reduction in trace-store write amps. Noted corner-case where tiny services with bursty traffic lost fairness—added token-bucket credits per customer as mitigation.
2026-02-10: Security and privacy check passed for emitted metadata schema. Updated dashboards for rollout monitoring: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/obs/sampling-feedback

2026-02-12: Started canary rollout to three regions behind feature flag. Monitoring hooks added to Console: per-route sample-rate diff, reservoir_utilization, feedback-controller-update-rate. Next: tune PID damping constants and add integration test that injects sustained error bursts to validate retention guarantees.
technical_notes: We prioritize zero allocations on hot path: ingress keeps a tiny ring counter and applies multiplier as integer math when possible.
Controller computes deltas not absolute rates to minimize size of push messages and reduce control-plane churn.
Hysteresis: require 3 consecutive windows above threshold before a downscale; immediate upscale on error spike to protect debugging.
Safety nets: per-service floor 1e-4 and ceiling 1.0; global emergency fallback to conservative reservoir when control plane unavailable.
Compatibility: works with existing tail-sampler and reservoir logic; we only adjust the upstream weight parameter consumed by samplers.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: controller oscillation causing sample-rate flapping. Mitigation: damped updates, minimum hold period, and rollout with gradual weight limits.
Risk: fairness regressions for low-volume customers. Mitigation: token-bucket credits and per-customer floor quotas before applying downscale.
Risk: increased control-plane load. Mitigation: delta encoding and push rate limit, and fallback to local conservative policy if control plane lag > 30s.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Canary regions show <=5% regression in error-trace retention for top 20 customers over 48h.
2) Overall sampled span emission reduced by >=25% for synthetic mix without increasing ingress p99 by >2%.
3) No allocator pressure increase on hot path; verified by flamegraphs from canary traffic.
4) Rollout runbook and Console dashboard widgets available and linked in Confluence doc.
